info.title: Amika API
info.description: HTTP API for Amika coding agents. Versioned per Google AIP-185.

bearerAuth.description: Bearer token: an Amika CLI session token or an Amika API key.

cookieAuth.name: wos-session
cookieAuth.description: Browser session cookie set after sign-in.

is_error.description: True when the turn failed. The failure is still a 200: `response` carries the agent CLI's own message (e.g. "Not logged in · Please run /login").

scope.description: Whether the key is scoped to the caller's organization or to the individual user who owns it.

name.description: Human-readable name for the API key.

scope.description: Scope of the key to create. Defaults to `organization`; pass `user` to mint a key owned by the calling user.

sandbox_ref.description: Source sandbox, by id or name; rejected if both match.

mode.description: scrub_and_delete (default): remove Amika-injected secrets (credential files + injected env vars) from the sandbox, capture the snapshot from the clean filesystem, then delete the source sandbox. full: capture everything as-is — including secrets — and keep the sandbox running.

resources.description: With `host_id`, the rig's resources, in place of a named `size`: 1 to 16 vCPUs, at least 64 MiB of memory in whole MiB, and a disk of at least 1 GiB. Requires `host_id`, and cannot be combined with `size`.

size.description: Providerless sandbox size (for example `a0.m`). Legacy names such as `m` and `medium` are also accepted. The provider is inferred from `provider` or the server default; when omitted, the size defaults to that provider's medium tier. With `host_id`, names one of the host's own sizes instead; a host rig with neither `size` nor `resources` gets 4 vCPUs, 8 GiB of memory and a 20 GiB disk.

name.description: Service name: a single DNS label, unique per sandbox.

port.description: Container port the service listens on.

url_scheme.description: URL scheme the gateway serves the service over.

url.description: The service's address on the rig's host, ending in `/`. It carries no credential.

header.description: The request header the token goes in, as `Bearer <token>`.
